processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sheets with different thickness were solution treated at 1100 °C for 1 h prior to cold rolling (parent process proc_solution-1100c-1h).

Sheets cold rolled to 30% thickness reduction after solution treatment; belongs to the low-to-medium reduction stage (10%–50%). Its microstructure is the Taylor-lattice-type low energy dislocation structure with refined slip bands (average slip band spacing ~231 nm).

structures.microstructure_counts: Taylor lattice of multiple slip bands; average slip band spacing 231 nm (30% reduction).

defects.type: dislocations / slip bands (planar glide, Taylor lattice)
dislocation pile-ups at intersections of slip bands

grain_structure.texture: almost random initially; Cu and S components increase at low-to-medium rolling reduction

phases_present.morphology: matrix containing multiple intersecting slip bands (Taylor lattice)
phases_present.texture: weak; Cu {112}<111> and S {123}<111> components increase at low-to-medium reductions

phases_present.morphology: nano-sized, uniformly distributed in the austenitic matrix

precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenitic matrix

structures.overall_structure: Typical low energy dislocation structure (LEDS) of Taylor-lattice type resulting from planar dislocation glide (stage I, 10%–50% rolling reduction); composed of multiple interacting slip bands whose spacing gradually refines. Microstructure is essentially austenite with uniformly distributed nano-sized κ'-carbides; grains remain roughly equiaxed.
